claim: PJM's current public postings add an effective end time of 21:00 EPT on 2026-10-13 to mandatory Pre-Emergency Load Management Reduction Actions 105561 and 105562. This establishes termination of the public dispatch intervals after seven hours and five hours respectively; it does not establish participant receipt, actual load reduction, delivered megawatts, workload migration, self-generation, penalties, or avoided escalation.

source.title: PJM Emergency Procedures Postings — Messages 105561 and 105562
source.observedState: Last Updated 10.13.2026 21:35:02 EPT; both actions show Effective End Time 21:00 EPT

source.title: Prior Quick_30 dispatch finding

falsifier: An authoritative PJM correction showing the 21:00 end times were erroneous, provisional, or did not represent release of the dispatch intervals would alter or falsify the termination claim.
firstUnsupportedArrow: Publicly posted end time -> every CSP and registered participant received the release -> participant obligations ceased -> performance telemetry established delivered MW -> the dispatch produced usable relief or avoided escalation
omissions: No expected or delivered megawatts, registration-level performance, telemetry, failures, penalties, or settlement records were retrieved.
No evidence distinguishes genuine load reduction from workload migration, deferred work, or behind-the-meter generation.
No explicit recipient acknowledgment chain or separate release message was retrieved.
No evidence connects the actions to data-center backup generation.
Ending the dispatch interval does not prove operating conditions were fully normal or that consequences were repaired.
EEA 1 and the October 14 DOE-resource notice remain separate active preparation states.

failures.detail: Registration-specific instructions and performance data remain inside DR Hub or other non-public operational records not retrieved here.
The public page shows end times but not who received, acknowledged, or acted on the release.

rivalHypotheses: The demand-response actions delivered sufficient relief and were released as conditions improved.
Conditions improved for unrelated reasons such as load decline, imports, generation availability, or transmission reconfiguration.
The dispatch ended on a planned product interval regardless of participant performance.
